offences.quote: Misusing Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools – In an assessment where the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools is not permitted, or permitted in only a specific manner as outlined in the relevant assessment brief, a student uses one or more AI tools to generate assessment content which is then submitted as their own original work.

Misusing Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools – In an assessment where the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools is not permitted, or permitted in only a specific manner as outlined in the relevant assessment brief, a student uses one or more AI tools to generate assessment content which is then submitted as their own original work.
Falsification of data or other research – where a student deliberately falsifies or fabricates results in order to support a thesis or argument.
Contracting/purchasing – where a student contracts or purchases from someone else, a piece of written work and submits it as their own original piece of written work.
Plagiarism – where a student uses, without appropriate acknowledgement, the work of other people and presents it as their own which may give an unfair advantage over others.
Taking unauthorised material into an assessment (including revision notes or unauthorised equipment) shall be regarded as a breach of Fixed-Time Assessment Regulations for Candidates

Collusion - where two or more people have worked together without permission to produce a piece of work which is then submitted for assessment as the work of only one person, which may give an unfair advantage over others.

Impersonating a student for the purposes of assessment attendance – where a student attends an assessment on behalf of another student with the intention of falsely representing their own work as having been produced by the impersonated person.

liability.quote: Intentional and unintentional acts of plagiarism will be construed as offences.
Poor academic practice will be addressed through the assessment of the work and will not result in disciplinary proceedings being brought against a student.

detection.quote: Written material in cases of alleged plagiarism would usually be expected to comprise of marked up original source documents in addition to the text matching software report.
A text-matching software report alone is usually insufficient to determine if plagiarism has occurred.
Academic or intellectual malpractice shall be established on the basis of academic judgement.

The Academic Offences Officer has the right to request an exceptional viva voce examination in cases where it is suspected that a student has contracted and/or purchased material for written assignments including project and dissertation work.

definitions.quote: Misusing Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools – In an assessment where the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools is not permitted, or permitted in only a specific manner as outlined in the relevant assessment brief, a student uses one or more AI tools to generate assessment content which is then submitted as their own original work.
Cheating - any academic or intellectual malpractice normally in assessments such as fixed-time assessments, fixed-window assessments or coursework which may give an unfair advantage over others.

Collusion - where two or more people have worked together without permission to produce a piece of work which is then submitted for assessment as the work of only one person, which may give an unfair advantage over others.
Contracting/purchasing – where a student contracts or purchases from someone else, a piece of written work and submits it as their own original piece of written work.
Plagiarism – where a student uses, without appropriate acknowledgement, the work of other people and presents it as their own which may give an unfair advantage over others.
Mitigation: evidence offered by a student to explain circumstances related to a disciplinary case which may if relevant lessen the severity of the penalty.
